# Glance
> Free, open-source desktop attention prediction, in development. Planned local ONNX inference for Windows and macOS.

Glance estimates early free-viewing attention from images. It does not record eyes or establish comprehension, memory, emotion or conversion. No Glance accuracy benchmark is established. Model licenses differ from application licensing.

## Documentation
- [Home](https://cgsudo.github.io/glance-attention/index.html): product and current status.
- [How it works](https://cgsudo.github.io/glance-attention/how-it-works.html): illustrated explanation.
- [Science](https://cgsudo.github.io/glance-attention/science.html): formulas, supplied benchmark references and limits.
- [Download](https://cgsudo.github.io/glance-attention/download.html): availability; no release artifact verified yet.
- [Integrations](https://cgsudo.github.io/glance-attention/integrations.html): planned CLI, localhost API and MCP contracts.
- [Comparisons](https://cgsudo.github.io/glance-attention/compare/index.html): attributed vendor facts and unknowns.
- [Citations](https://cgsudo.github.io/glance-attention/citations.html): sources and license boundaries.

## Guides
- [Is predictive eye tracking accurate?](https://cgsudo.github.io/glance-attention/guides/is-predictive-eye-tracking-accurate.html): Understand what a 94% headline can mean, human agreement ceilings, saliency metrics and the limits of predicting gaze from a design.
- [How to use an attention heatmap for landing pages](https://cgsudo.github.io/glance-attention/guides/attention-heatmap-for-landing-pages.html): Check a landing page headline, image and CTA with predicted attention. Follow a practical review workflow and learn what heatmaps cannot prove.
- [The squint test for designers: value study vs model](https://cgsudo.github.io/glance-attention/guides/squint-test-for-designers.html): Use the painter’s squint test to inspect visual hierarchy, then compare it with a saliency model. Learn where each helps and where both stop.
